title: What a Ticket Is
hook: The paper is not the lesson.
scene: Clear cold midday on a side street after the stop. Dunn has already walked back. A slip of paper sits on the cracked pink dash — numbers, a box, a signature line, no lecture. The remnant is gone. The paper is a record of what you did, and a date to answer it. It is not permission to keep the habit. It is not a debt you pay in noise. It is not the end of the run unless you make it one.
decision: The paper is on the dash and he is gone. What is it?

options.text: Proof the stop is over — you can drive like you did before
options.result: You treat the slip as a receipt. The next block gets the same number. The paper was a record, not a reset. Dunn does not have to be there for the habit to still be the habit.

options.text: A fine you can ignore until someone else stops you
options.result: You fold it into the glove box and forget the date. The record does not forget. Ignoring it is a second problem with a first one's name on it.

options.text: A record you answer by the date, and a habit you change now
options.result: You read the date. You put the slip with the clipboard later. You roll at a number the paper would not write again. The stop stays a stop. The habit does not get a sequel.

options.text: A mark on you that means you should not drive the rest of the day
options.result: You shut the Menace off in the middle of a run because paper felt like a verdict. A ticket is not a suspension unless it says so. You spent a block the Core still needed.

debrief: A ticket is a record with a date to answer. Change the habit now. You saved the habit a sequel.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part two
source.teaching_target: A ticket is a written record that must be answered by the date; it is not permission to keep the behavior and not an automatic suspension.
